--- title: "Datasets" subtitle: "What each dataset is, where it came from, and what is wrong with it" --- Defects are stated plainly here rather than softened. A dataset's known problems are the first thing a reader needs, because they bound what any result computed from it can mean. ## OPMD binder sequences ::: {#7e383059 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=2} `data/opmd_binders_clean.csv` — **10 binders** against 4 targets (IL10, IL6, LCN2, MMP9), 20 columns. In-house wet-lab records, consolidated from three source spreadsheets (a decision tree, 'Sheet4', and a marker tracker) into one row per binder, with sequences, expression conditions and outcomes. Consumed by the physicochemical track ([2026-11-05T0754Z_physchem_descriptors-10binders](runs/2026-11-05T0754Z_physchem_descriptors-10binders/)); recorded there at SHA-256 `d08115c5353c948d…`, 3896 bytes. ::: ::: ::: {#39d6ff28 .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
binder_id target sequence_length has_his_tag expression soluble_fraction elisa_result data_quality_flag
0 IL6P233 IL6 90 FALSE no NA NA ok
1 IL6AD15 IL6 90 FALSE yes supernatant positive ok
2 IL10R2 IL10 105 FALSE no NA negative ok
3 IL10NB5 IL10 268 FALSE yes pellet pending ok
4 IL10NB1 IL10 130 TRUE yes pellet pending ok
5 LCN2_B1 LCN2 100 TRUE yes supernatant positive conditions conflict between sheets
6 LCN2_B5 LCN2 105 TRUE yes supernatant positive ok
7 MMP9B7 MMP9 87 FALSE yes pellet negative ok
8 MMP9B9 MMP9 128 FALSE yes supernatant negative ok
9 MMP9B17 MMP9 173 FALSE yes supernatant NA sequence reconstructed (hyphens removed)
``` ::: ::: ### Known defects ::: {#706939e7 .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=4} **Far too small for supervised learning.** 10 binders with 2 non-expressers and 3 insoluble cases. This cannot support training on embeddings or on anything else; see the [open question](decisions.qmd#labelled-data). **Unresolved source conflict in LCN2_B1.** The source sheets disagree on host strain and IPTG concentration (decision tree: BL21 with 0.5 mM; marker tracker: Rosetta with 0.3 mM). Both fields carry the literal value `CONFLICT`. No value is imputed, and the physicochemical pipeline reads all metadata as text so the sentinel cannot corrupt numeric parsing of other rows. Temperature and duration do agree. [Open question](decisions.qmd#lcn2-conditions). **Rows carrying a data-quality flag: 2.** ::: ::: ::: {#45d8df3f .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
binder_id data_quality_flag notes
5 LCN2_B1 conditions conflict between sheets UNRESOLVED CONFLICT: Decision Tree records BL2...
9 MMP9B17 sequence reconstructed (hyphens removed) Decision Tree copy carried five spurious hyphe...
``` ::: ::: ::: {#e84b89e7 .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=6} **Experimental conditions are not uniform.** 2 of 10 binders were tested under multiple conditions, recorded as multi-valued text (for example `temperature_C` = `37; 30`, `iptg_mM` = `0.3; 0.5; 1.0`). A binder that failed at one condition is not comparable to one that succeeded at another, and the table does not record which condition produced the reported outcome. **Outcome labels are partly subjective.** `expression` and `soluble_fraction` derive from gel inspection. One binder's faint band prompted a western blot that came back negative, so the numeric label and the visual impression disagree. ELISA results include `pending` and `NA`. **Two sequences were repaired during cleaning.** MMP9B17's sequence was reconstructed by removing five spurious hyphens present in one source copy; removing them reproduces the other sheet's sequence exactly. IL10R2's name carried a stray backtick. Both are recorded in `notes`. **Mixed construct classes.** The set contains de-novo helical designs and antibody-derived VH / VH-linker-VH nanobody formats. These differ systematically in length, charge and composition, so any apparent grouping by outcome is confounded with format. ::: ::: Validation is applied on read rather than assumed: standard amino acids only, and the declared `sequence_length` must match the real length. All {python} f"{len(binders)}" rows currently pass. ## bench20 complex selection ::: {#c0de0b25 .cell execution_count=7} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=7} `bench20/selection.tsv` — **20 two-chain protein–protein complexes** drawn from the local PDBBind general protein–protein set ([2026-10-30T0000Z_interface-kd_complex-selection](runs/2026-10-30T0000Z_interface-kd_complex-selection/)). X-ray only, each chain over 50 residues, exact Kd (not an inequality), selection seed `20261030`. Resolution 1.10–3.00 Å; deposition years 1998–2019. ::: ::: ::: {#24f60d06 .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html}

A rank correlation over this set is partly measuring agreement between heterogeneous experiments. [Open question](decisions.qmd#pdbbind-recuration). **31 of 40 chains have SEQRES/ATOM length differences**, meaning the submitted sequence contains residues that are absent from the crystal structure — up to 113 extra residues in 4bkx. Predictions and reference structures are therefore not models of identical molecules, which puts a floor under achievable DockQ for those cases. **Kd values are inherited from PDBBind annotations**, not re-read from the primary literature. Index parent-publication references were checked for uniqueness, but the measurements themselves were not independently verified. **One self-template.** 3w8h's own PDB entry appeared among its AlphaFold template hits (single-chain templates), so its prediction is not fully blind. ::: ::: ## AlphaFold predictions and derived structures ::: {#b0f4f816 .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=10} `alphafold3_server/metadata/af3_confidence.tsv` — per-model pTM, ipTM and ranking score for **100 models** (20 complexes x 5 models) ([2026-11-03T0000Z_interface-kd_af3-predictions](runs/2026-11-03T0000Z_interface-kd_af3-predictions/)). ipTM 0.15–0.94. **The `server_job_id` column is empty**: the AlphaFold Server downloads do not include job identifiers, so individual predictions cannot be traced back to their submissions. Provenance stops at the job request files. **Terms of use are unresolved** and block publication of anything derived from these predictions. [Open question](decisions.qmd#alphafold-terms). ::: ::: Large artefacts are deliberately **not** stored in `runs/` or served by this site. They are recorded in the relevant manifest by path, hash and size, and left where they live: ::: {#3defd7eb .cell execution_count=12} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown execution_count=12} Also on local disk and not in the site: `alphafold3_server/predictions/` (about 709 MB of CIF and converted PDB models) and `bench20/work/` (about 197 MB of relaxed structures, Rosetta score files and PLIP XML). `pdbbind/` holds 2,798 supplied complex structures and is git-ignored. These must be present locally to re-execute the interface track; the site records only their location and the summary tables derived from them. ::: ::: ## Dataset provenance summary ::: {#ff180ede .cell execution_count=13} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ```{=html}
